description: Diagnose the resolved vault's health: whether TaskForge/Settings/dialect.json and TaskForge/Settings/spaces.json are present (with their generated_at/app_version provenance), whether the vault root is actually writable (a real create+delete probe, not a permissions guess), and any spaces.json defect (absent, unparseable, or a schema_version this build can't interpret). Read-only by DEFAULT. Run it first when a tool reports a vault-resolution error or space operations behave unexpectedly — the warnings tell you (and the user) exactly what to fix. Pass fix:true to also REPAIR what the vault's own evidence allows before reporting (today: regenerate an absent or settings-stale dialect.json from settings.json — the headless equivalent of `taskforge doctor --fix`, and the remedy for the 'dialect.json is stale relative to settings.json' warning when there is no GUI to open). A quarantined dialect is never auto-cleared. The `repaired` field lists what was done; `[]` means nothing needed doing.

fix.description:
Repair what can be repaired from evidence already in the vault before
reporting — the MCP twin of the CLI's `doctor --fix`, so an agent on
either surface has the same remedy. Today: regenerate an absent or
settings-stale `dialect.json` from `settings.json`. A quarantined
dialect is never auto-cleared. Default `false` — `doctor` stays
read-only unless a caller asks for the repair. What was repaired comes
back in the result's `repaired` field (`[]` = nothing needed doing).

rebuild_index.description:
Discard the persisted scan index (vault-index-northstar spec
Decision 3) — the MCP twin of the CLI's `doctor --rebuild-index`,
the "I don't trust it" button. The next scan rebuilds it cold.
Default `false`; what happened comes back in `index_rebuilt`. The
index's current state (age, entry count, schema version, path) is
always in the `index` field, with or without this flag.

name: doctor
